content:
The image shows a citrus fruit (lemon/orange) with approximately two-thirds of its surface covered in a dense, powdery olive-green/grey fungal growth, while the remaining portion retains its normal yellow-orange color. The fungal coating is compact and uniform in texture, consistent with the description of Whisker Mold — specifically the white-to-olive-green spore masses (conidia) covering the fruit surface.

Key visual evidence matching Whisker_Mold:
- Citrus fruit host (orange/lemon)
- Dense, compact fungal growth covering most of the fruit surface
- Olive-green/grey coloration of the spore mass (characteristic of *Myceliophthora* or similar whisker mold fungi)
- Powdery/granular texture matching the described cylindrical or obpyriform conidia
- Clear boundary between infected and healthy fruit tissue
